Explanation: The core value unit is the agreed freelance service: either a pre-packaged Offer or custom work defined through a Project proposal.
PeoplePerHour operates the marketplace, reviews freelancer applications, manages matching, WorkStream, escrow, disputes and platform rules.
The platform has to connect a buyer need with a freelancer who can deliver the work.
More successful jobs create marketplace fees, repeat relationships and stronger liquidity.
Poor work, fraud, payment problems or weak matching can make buyers and freelancers leave.
PeoplePerHour organizes Offers, Projects, proposals, escrow, invoices and marketplace fees.
Transaction Flows: ← Consumer · Buy / Brief — A buyer either purchases a ready-made Offer or posts a Project brief and funds the agreed work. | → Consumer · Offers / Match — PeoplePerHour presents packaged services, freelancer profiles and proposals that fit the buyer need. | ← Provider · Offer / Proposal — Freelancers publish Offers or submit custom proposals for Projects. | → Provider · Jobs / Payout — PeoplePerHour routes accepted work through WorkStream and releases cleared earnings after invoicing and escrow. | ← Partner · Payment Rails — Payment partners process buyer payments and freelancer withdrawal rails used around the escrow workflow.

Explanation: Freelancer applications are reviewed and marketplace rules govern listings, proposals, payments and conduct.
PeoplePerHour uses search, category discovery and Phoenix AI to help buyers find suitable freelancers.
The platform reviews users, matches work, supports WorkStream communication, holds escrow and handles disputes.
Core resources include freelancer profiles, ratings, skills, job history, buyer briefs, WorkStream data and marketplace software.
Buyers are businesses and individuals that need freelance work, especially small and medium-sized businesses.
Buyers want a suitable freelancer to complete a task or project without hiring a full-time employee.
Buyers can choose between ready-made Offers, proposals to a custom Project, or direct contact with a freelancer.
Buyers can struggle to define the job, judge quality or know whether a freelancer will deliver on time.
Buyers purchase an Offer or fund escrow after accepting a custom proposal.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Buy / Brief — A buyer either purchases a ready-made Offer or posts a Project brief and funds the agreed work. | ← Owner · Offers / Match — PeoplePerHour presents packaged services, freelancer profiles and proposals that fit the buyer need. | → Provider · Work / Feedback — The buyer provides requirements and feedback while the freelancer delivers the agreed service.

Explanation: Buyers compare skills, ratings, portfolios, timing, proposals and price.
Buyers use the PeoplePerHour marketplace, search and Phoenix AI to discover talent.
Buyers can post a Project, buy an Offer, contact freelancers, review work and release payment.
Buyers bring the problem, project requirements, budget, files, feedback and payment.
Freelancers provide skills such as design, writing, development, marketing, administration and many other business services.
Freelancers want to find paying clients and turn their skills into repeatable income.
The marketplace provides access to buyers, repeat relationships and payment protection through escrow.
Freelancers compete for attention, proposals and ratings and can spend time applying without winning work.
Freelancers publish fixed-price Offers, submit proposals and deliver custom work through WorkStream.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Offer / Proposal — Freelancers publish Offers or submit custom proposals for Projects. | ← Owner · Jobs / Payout — PeoplePerHour routes accepted work through WorkStream and releases cleared earnings after invoicing and escrow. | ← Consumer · Work / Feedback — The buyer provides requirements and feedback while the freelancer delivers the agreed service.

Explanation: Freelancers are reviewed at application and then build reputation through ratings, work history and marketplace performance.
Freelancers use profiles, Offers, proposal tools, saved searches and WorkStream to reach buyers.
Freelancers package services, submit proposals, communicate, deliver work and raise invoices.
Their key resources are skills, portfolio, availability, reputation, proposals and completed work.
Third-party payment providers help PeoplePerHour collect buyer payments and move freelancer payouts.
Payment partners provide regulated payment rails between buyers, PeoplePerHour and freelancers.
More marketplace transactions create more payment and payout volume for these providers.
Payment fraud, chargebacks, compliance checks and settlement delays create cost and friction.
Providers process card payments, account transfers and freelancer withdrawals around PeoplePerHour escrow.
Transaction Flows: → Owner · Payment Rails — Payment partners process buyer payments and freelancer withdrawal rails used around the escrow workflow.

Explanation: Payment methods depend on country, currency and supported payment or withdrawal provider.
PeoplePerHour connects to payment providers and banking rails to receive and distribute funds.
Partners authorize payments, transfer funds and perform payment-compliance and security checks.
Their resources include card networks, banking connections, regulated payment infrastructure and fraud controls.
